title: an inline callback argument may abort with panic(...) without needing a failure contract
notes: specification/failures.mdx §Panic Does Not Widen a Return Type: 'Calling `panic(...)` MUST NOT force a function's return type to widen into `Result<A, Panic>`.' and 'A function that validates an argument, refuses a forgery, or asserts an invariant MUST therefore be able to abort with `panic(...)` while keeping a plain return type.' docs/DECISIONS.md carries the matching Locked entry ('Calling `panic(...)` does not widen a return type into `Result<A, Panic>` … the prohibition is on the compiler forcing it'). `E` is the expected-error channel (reference/function-channels.mdx) and a panic is not an expected error, so a construct that aborts with `panic(...)` keeps whatever return type it declares. A callback that carries a checked failure across a value edge needs a spelled contract — that is SMITHERS1303, and it is untouched: see the eleven refusals in 07-must-consume. A panic is not a checked failure, so it has no channel to lose at the boundary and the callback needs no contract. Measured before the rule landed as SMITHERS1303 at the callback, plus SMITHERS1101 in the annotated spelling. This case and the SMITHERS1303 family are the two halves of the same boundary and must both stay green.
